title: “Sunblock” and “100% protection” are off-limits
notes: Dewlane Woche 1 (Produktion 01.11.2026), Vorlage 1.0, Qualitätsmaßstab Testvideo Q1. Thema aus dem Kalender: Aussagen wie Sunblock, völliger Schutz oder Schutz für den ganzen Tag sollen nicht verwendet werden; die FDA sagt, es gibt keinen wasserfesten Sonnenschutz. Nur Aussagen aus den Kalenderquellen (geöffnet 01.11.2026). Englische Fassung sprachlich angepasst.

layout.description: Is 100% protection real? The US Food and Drug Administration is just as clear: there's no such thing as a waterproof sunscreen. All sunscreens eventually wash off, and it advises reapplying at least every two hours.

beats.spoken: No sunscreen can filter out all UV radiation, says the European Commission.
That's in its 2006 recommendation on sunscreen products. Even products with very high protection against UVB and UVA can't give complete protection against the health risks of UV radiation.

So certain claims shouldn't be made: one hundred percent protection, like “sunblock”, “sunblocker” or “complete protection”. And nothing suggesting you never need to reapply, like “all-day protection”.

Instead, warnings should make clear there's no hundred percent protection. The recommendation gives examples: don't stay in the sun too long, even with sunscreen, and keep babies and small children out of direct sunlight.

items.title: Not too long in the sun

beats.spoken: The US Food and Drug Administration is just as clear: there's no such thing as a waterproof sunscreen. All sunscreens eventually wash off, and it advises reapplying at least every two hours.
For you, that means: be wary of the word sunblock. Sunscreen is one building block, not a force field, and shade and clothing are part of it.
